title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement_md:
Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

### Input and Output
Your code is a function `solution`. Return the value exactly as expected; the judge compares with strict equality.

### Examples
**Example 1:**
```
Longest Increasing Subsequence(10, 9, 2, 5, 3, 7, 101, 18) -> 4
```

**Example 2:**
```
Longest Increasing Subsequence(0, 1, 0, 3, 2, 3) -> 4
```
concept_md: dp[i] = length of the best increasing sequence ending at i, reused by later indexes — classic O(n²) DP. Recognise it when a longest/main/best result depends on an ordering and earlier choices constrain later ones.
hints: An element can only extend sequences that end before it with a smaller value — think about what a single number knows.
dp[i] is the answer to 'longest sequence ending exactly at i'; build it from every earlier smaller value.
dp = [1]*n; for i: for j<i: if nums[j]<nums[i]: dp[i]=max(dp[i],dp[j]+1); answer = max(dp)
